summary: A sound stage-1 rewrite. The parity profile shows Marlin at roughly 1-1.6 TB/s on the three small-M shapes (41.1/107.6/150.9 us against 11.4/37.3/52.5 us floors), and the design fixes both measured causes of the triton-w13 failure: the idle grid, and dequant costing about 15 ALU ops per weight. No rules problem. The biggest risk is that each work item's inner K loop is too short to pipeline (4 BLOCK_K steps for w13, only 2 for w2, with num_stages=4), so a persistent loop over items may expose a full memory latency per item.
justification: Mechanism: at bs=1 the two Marlin calls move about 1.93 x 28.3 MB = 54.6 MB in 41.1 us (~1.33 TB/s). The triton-w13 run's profile gives the split: Marlin w2 alone was 18.2 us for ~18 MB (~1.0 TB/s), so w13 was ~22.9 us (inferred by subtraction, not measured). At bs=8 Marlin is ~107.6 us for ~178 MB (~1.65 TB/s). That leaves 2.5-3.6x of headroom per shape, and the stage-1 targets (55-65% of HBM) are modest. The floors match TASK.md exactly: w13 is 8192 x 2048 B plus 8192 x 256 B of scales = 18.9 MB, w2 is 9.4 MB. The touched-expert counts are consistent with the 11.4/37.3/52.5 us floors. The expected directions are consistent: bs<=16 is faster and bs=32/128/256 stay on the byte-identical Marlin path as controls. If every target is met, the headline is about (80.2/60 x 152/105 x 191.4/125)^(1/6) = ~1.20x, so it is readable far beyond the 1.5-2.5% run-to-run drift. The milestone is directly readable: the new kernels appear by name in top_kernels per shape, against the Marlin line. Caveat: the incumbent's w13/w2 split at bs=16 is not measured anywhere, so only the combined 150.9 us is a valid yardstick there. Design checks: (1) Parallelism. 512 items per touched expert per GEMM over a 528-CTA persistent grid gives about 2 items per CTA at bs=1 and 9 at bs=16. This fixes the ~30/32-empty static grid. (2) Bit-placement dequant is correct. Codes e=1..3 land on 2^-14 x {1,1.5}, {2,3}, {4,6}, and the 0.5 code lands as the fp16 subnormal 2^-15. One fp32 multiply by sf x 2^14 (at most 7.3e6) is exact, and the cvt to bf16 is exact (product of at most 6 significant bits). nvfp4.py draws block scales with log2 ~ N(7, 0.4), so nothing approaches a range edge. The cost is about 3 lane-ops per weight (place, cvt f16->f32, fmul, half a cvt bf16x2, plus the sf broadcast). That is close to the self-quoted 3.5 ops/weight full-HBM budget but well inside the ~6 available at the 55% target. (3) tl.dot with M=16 uses mma.sync, not wgmma, which is fine at this M. (4) Bytes in flight (~12 MB) are about 2x Little's law if the pipeline actually fills. WEAKEST LINK: Triton software-pipelines only the innermost loop. A w13 item covers K=1024 (4 iterations of 256) and a w2 item covers K=512 (2 iterations) with num_stages=4. Each item therefore runs a cold prologue and drains before the next item's loads are issued, and w2 can never hold more than 2 stages in flight. At bs=16 (~9 items per CTA) this exposes about 9 memory latencies per CTA, and only the 4-CTA/SM co-residency hides them. Fix options: flatten item x k_step into one linear tl.range loop so prefetch crosses item boundaries, or give w2 SPLIT_K=4 (K=1024 per item) with BLOCK_N=32 to keep the item count. The second weakest link is the ticket-counter split-K reduce, which is unproven on this judge's Triton; the in-flight bf16 semaphore kernels are the first test of it.
confounders: sglang-marlin-path-parity (the base and the only landed hypothesis): it cannot be absent. The rewrite reuses its moe_align_block_size(local_ids, ., 32) over the 32-expert bank, at block 16 instead of 8. Align time at block 16 vs 8 moves by under 1 us and shows as its own profile row, so it cannot flip the sign of a GEMV result.

The at::native glue (reduce_kernel<512> ~5.6 us, elementwise ~5.4 us and others at bs=1) is not part of the w13 Marlin wrapper: it persisted in the triton-w13 run. If some of it belongs to the w2 wrapper, it disappears with this change and inflates the layer-level gain. Judge the milestone on the new kernels' own time, not on the layer delta.
interference: No companions. This is a rewrite judged on its replaced kernels' own time per shape, which the profile reports directly. The only landed hypothesis is the base itself, so an ab-revert would return to the starter, and the align knob it carries is not a meaningful tune axis. The three untouched shapes (bs=32/128/256) are built-in controls for drift. The natural follow-up is stage 2: flattened or retuned SPLIT_K, and silu fused into the w13 last-CTA epilogue.
rules_flags: No rules problem found. The second weight copy is the same NVFP4 bytes (a lossless byte-order permutation is allowed under 'repack/compress losslessly'). Global scales stay fp32 and are applied in the epilogue. Activations are bf16 in and out, with fp32 only in the accumulator and scratch.

The scratch and counters are workspace, not cached data: partials are fully rewritten every call before they are read, and the counters self-reset. Keep the w13 and w2 counter arrays separate (or reset both), and make sure the prepare() self-test leaves them at zero.

The small_path fallback flag is decided in prepare() from weight-only synthetic data and a fixed torch.Generator, so it does not branch on inputs. Print the self-test's rel-L2 loudly in both outcomes: a silent fallback would make stage 1 look 'flat' and waste the run.
No host syncs. The live-block count must be read on device from n_padded (a runtime loop bound inside the kernel), never with .item(). Use fixed constexpr configs and no triton.autotune.
Do not convert x to fp16 to make an fp16 x fp16 dot possible: that changes activation precision where SGLang keeps bf16. Keep the bf16 dot as written.
open_questions: Memory ordering of the ticket: a scalar tl.atomic_add with sem='acq_rel' orders only the issuing thread's stores. Put tl.debug_barrier() between the partial stores and the ticket. In the last CTA, after the acquire, put another barrier and read the other splits' partials with cache_modifier='.cg' (L2, bypassing L1), or L1-stale data can be summed.

How does moe_align_block_size(local_ids, 16, 32) lay out remote (-1) slots and blocks? Marlin with is_ep=True skips blocks whose block_experts entry is -1 and masks sorted_ids >= M*8. The work-list decode must replicate both checks, or a remote block will read expert -1's weights.

w13 gathers x[slot // 8] (top_k=8 semantics) and w2 gathers cache2[slot] (top_k=1). cache3 aliases cache1's storage, as in the base. Confirm that the gate/up row order of the raw w13 (gate rows [0, I), up rows [I, 2I)) matches what silu_and_mul expects of cache1 as Marlin wrote it.

Several queued hypotheses build on the regressed triton-w13 kernel: triton-w2-grouped-gemv-small-m, triton-w13-silu-epilogue and possibly triton-small-m-threshold-32. Should they be retired or re-based on this line? The rewrite's own risk (f) says not to stack them.
align-256-experts-below-128 (p1, queued) changes the align call this path reuses. If it lands first, the rewrite's base and its align row move. Decide the order.
